parts.text: A student investigates the image produced by a converging lens. He uses the equipment shown in Fig. 3.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student sets the distance u between the illuminated triangular object and the lens to 20.0 cm. He moves the screen until a sharp image of the illuminated triangular object is seen on the screen. Briefly describe one technique to obtain an image on the screen which is as sharp as possible in this experiment. ................................................................................................................................................... ............................................................................................................................................. [1]

ms.label: 3(a)
ms.text: move screen backwards and forwards / move screen slowly

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) The screen is shown full size in Fig. 3.2. Measure, and record in the first line of Table 3.1, the height h I of the image on the screen, as shown in Fig. 3.2. Table 3.1 u / cm h I / cm D / 1 cm 20.0 25.0 2.8 0.36 30.0 2.0 0.50 35.0 1.6 0.63 40.0 1.2 0.83 [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) For distance u = 20.0 cm, calculate, and record in Table 3.1, a value D. Use your value of h I from Table 3.1 and the equation: D = 1 h I . [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student repeats the procedure for u = 25.0 cm, u = 30.0 cm, u = 35.0 cm and u = 40.0 cm. His results are shown in Table 3.1. Plot a graph of u / cm (y‑axis) against D / 1 cm (x‑axis). Start the axes at the origin (0,0). Draw a best‑fit straight line. [4]

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
graph:
•
axes labelled with quantity and unit
•
appropriate scales (occupying at least ½ grid)
•
plots all correct to ½ small square, precise plots
•
well judged line and thin line

parts.label: i
parts.text: (d) (i) From your graph, determine u 0 , the value of u when D is zero. u 0 = .................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = .......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(d)(ii)
ms.text: G recorded and triangle method shown on graph

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) The illuminated object is shown full size in Fig. 3.3. Measure and record the height h O of the illuminated triangular object shown in Fig. 3.3. h O = .......................................................... cm Calculate the focal length f of the lens. Use your value of h O , your value of G from (d)(ii) and the equation: f = G h O × k, where k = 1.0 cm 2 . f = .......................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text:
hO present and
f in range 13.5 to 16.5 (cm)

ms.label: 3(f)
